title: Save and recognise file types
summary: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file.
introduction: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain save and recognise file types
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A file extension helps the editor choose language support. Saving changes writes them to disk; an unsaved tab can differ from the saved file.

blocks.code:
index.html -> HTML
style.css -> CSS
notes.txt -> plain text
blocks.title: Save and recognise file types

blocks.text: The extension communicates the file type. The editor's language mode can also be selected manually.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Save a small HTML page and open it in a browser.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A file named page.html.txt is still a text file by its final extension.
For more detail later, use this [VS Code further reading](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/getstarted/getting-started).
